chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman whose husband was absent, so he returned while she was in Itikaaf (seclusion) by her husband's permission. She exited from the mosque to her house when news of his arrival reached her, and she prepared herself for her husband until he had intercourse with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she had exited the mosque before three days had passed, and she had not stipulated a specific duration in her Itikaaf, then upon her is the penalty of the one who performs Zihaar.'

key_terms.اعْتِكَافٌ: Itikaaf: Seclusion in a mosque for worship
key_terms.الْمُظَاهِرِ: The one who performs Zihaar (a specific type of divorce/penalty)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a woman leaving the mosque early during Itikaaf if her husband returns?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of Itikaaf for women, specifically addressing the scenario where a wife leaves the mosque upon her husband's return before the customary three-day period concludes. The ruling imposes the penalty of Zihaar (ظِهَار) if no specific duration was stipulated, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that early departure without valid excuse incurs a specific expiation akin to the divorce form. This highlights the intersection of marital rights and ritual purity obligations in Ja'fari jurisprudence.
